correctness.rationale: The exact configurations and closed-neighborhood token-adjacency definition were reconstructed from RESULT.md. For any dominating set, one-A configurations select edges P on the B part; every triangle of the complementary graph Q has to occur as a selected all-B configuration. Deleting one Q edge per such triangle leaves a triangle-free graph, so Mantel yields |P|+|T|>=C(n,2)-floor(n²/4). The supplied four disjoint witness families use same-half B pairs with a0, all pairs of A-indices >=1 with any B vertex, {a0,a1,b} outside a fixed three-set R, and R itself; direct layer-by-layer adjacency verifies domination for all m>=2. The construction has the exact stated size, giving fixed-m squeezing. Independently enumerated 23 small (m,n) cases from graph adjacency; that test is not the infinite proof. No exact lower-order domination number is established.

value.rationale: Determining a sharp leading-order quadratic coefficient for ordinary domination on the first nontrivial three-token complete-bipartite family, with explicit O_m(n) error and a precise Mantel obstruction, resolves a natural asymptotic question beyond the known two-token case; it does not pretend to settle exact finite values.

final_claim: For all integers 2<=m<=n,n>=4, the ordinary domination number of F_3(K_{m,n}) lies between q(n)=C(n,2)-floor(n²/4) and q(n)+(C(m-1,2)+1)n-2; for each fixed m it is asymptotic to n²/4.
